text:
Alex Chen: heads-up: after yesterday's kernel-scheduling tweak p99 for short-seq requests climbed from ~75ms -> ~94ms. digging in host stack now.
Maria Gomez: yikes. which scheduling change exactly?
Alex Chen: scheduler now prefers packing more requests per-kernel-invocation to amortize kernel setup (aim: throughput). it increased burstiness on host preproc (tokenize+frame) and bumped small writev count.
Samir Patel: can you share the flame and syscall counts?
Alex Chen: flamegraph (top functions) excerpt:
```
parse_request_frame  30%
writev_aggregate     22%
tokenize_short       10%
kv_cache_lock        9%
malloc               7%
```
Syscalls per-second: before 420/s -> after 760/s. writev calls up ~1.8x.
Jordan Lee: that matches an increase in small I/O bursts. did the streaming-chunker size change?
Alex Chen: we also enabled adaptive-slicing (min_chunk=128) which multiplied fragments for short payloads. combination of denser kernel packing + smaller slices = more frequent writes and more KV churn.
Maria Gomez: any kv hitrate change?
Alex Chen: hitrate dipped from 0.88 -> 0.72 in the test window. eviction pressure on hot shards increased. background compaction threads started stealing cycles.
Samir Patel: quick theory: heavier kernel packing increases CPU time in compute threads, delaying host preproc completion. in-flight tokens queue up and are flushed as many small frames; also KV mutex contention spikes. two mitigations: 1) increase slice size for short payloads; 2) coalesce adjacent writev entries at host side; 3) add soft affinity so batching prefers requests with same kv-shard.
Maria Gomez: let's A/B. Plan: A) roll back packing heuristic (pack_limit=8->4), keep adaptive-slicing. B) keep packing and raise min_chunk to 512 and enable writev_coalesce. measure p99, writev_rate, kv_evictions.
Alex Chen: launching canaries now. config A: PACK_LIMIT=4; config B: MIN_CHUNK=512, WRITEV_COALESCE=1.
perf-bot: canary-start: 10% traffic each.
Alex Chen: quick results after 20m:
- A (less packing): p99 short-seq 78ms, writev_rate -20%, kv_evictions -30%
- B (bigger chunk + coalesce): p99 short-seq 73ms, writev_rate -54%, kv_evictions -65%
Jordan Lee: so B looks best for tail. but what about throughput and long-seq latency?
Alex Chen: throughput (RPS) stable across both. long-seq p50/p99 unchanged for A, slight p99 +3ms for B (within noise).
Samir Patel: B introduces more host-side buffering to merge writes; need to ensure we don't violate streaming latency SLO for ultra-low-latency clients. what was streaming tail for the first chunk?
Alex Chen: first-chunk latency p50 same, p99 for first-chunk +5ms on B. we think it's acceptable; still within client SLO.
Maria Gomez: long-term fixes: 1) kernel selector should expose a shard-affinity hint so batcher can prefer co-located requests; 2) offload KV maintenance to a dedicated low-priority threadpool that backpressures less; 3) refine adaptive-slicer to avoid excessive fragmentation for short payloads when kernel packing is high.
Jordan Lee: agree. also add runtime checks to prevent enabling high-packing when kv.hitrate < 0.8 or writev_rate > 500/s.
Samir Patel: code snippets for rollout guard:
```
if (kv.hitrate < 0.8 || host.writev_rate > 500) {
  enable_high_packing = false;
}
```
Alex Chen: implemented guard and will run staged rollout for PACK_LIMIT=8 behind it. instrumentation added: writev_coalesce_hits, avg_writev_iovec, kv_hot_evictions, kernel_pack_size_hist.
perf-bot: nightly-report: config-B (coalesce+512B) shows best tail reduction for short sequences. writev_syscalls reduced 52%, kv_evictions down 61%, short-seq p99 -12ms.
Maria Gomez: next actions: 1) keep coalesce+512B as default for now; 2) rework kernel selector to emit affinity hint by end of week; 3) schedule KV threadpool refactor (low priority) but important.
Jordan Lee: please add validation jobs that simulate high small-client mix and ensure guards prevent high-packing.
Alex Chen: on it. uploading traces + microbench results to the ticket. TL;DR: kernel packing optimization improved compute efficiency but exposed host-side IO/KV bottlenecks; host-level coalescing + chunk sizing + affinity guards fix tail. :white_check_mark:
